Admiring and honorific: chosen over 'bravery' it ennobles the courage as chivalrous and dashing, the word of medal citations.

To get rid of someone casts them as a nuisance to be disposed of; 'got rid of her two most deserving daughters' is ironic precisely because the word is dismissive, and a learner choosing it over 'part with' or 'send away' is signalling contempt for the thing removed.

Abhorrence names an intensely condemnatory attitude (hate plus disgust) toward its object, directly parallel to 'abominable' which this same packet correctly marks a connotation candidate, so a learner needs to know it signals strong condemnation rather than neutral description.
